Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We ran the preliminary load tests and the results flagged a repeated 95th percentile latency bump in our peak window when batch sizes grow beyond the 8k token horizon. Given the nature of our customer flows, we need a temporary operational carve-in for latency that doesn't immediately trigger the standard monthly credit bands while we complete our optimization work.

Specifically, we are asking: can Redwood provide a 60-day grace period where p95 latency breaches up to +40% are treated as "operational degraded state" (with diagnostics and mitigations) rather than an automatic service credit trigger? We'd also like to harmonize the monthly credit mechanics so that the remedy for blended uptime reduction during that 60-day pilot is capped at a flat monthly credit not exceeding 10% of our committed spend, rather than the sliding bands in the draft SLA.

I realize this is an ask outside standard templates — happy to provide the test logs and a short note from our infra team. Can we get a proposed approach from you and your legal team by end of week?

Samira —

Thanks for the detail and for sending the log extract. I dug into the CSV with Connor and have a couple of quick thoughts. We can support a limited operational grace period, but we need clear telemetry gating (traces + KV cache warmup signals) and a rollback path — otherwise the exception can cause quality regressions for other customers under the same dedicated pool.

Proposed near-term approach:
- 60-day pilot (as requested) where p95 latency breaches between +20% and +40% are classified as "operational degraded state" if accompanied by an agreed diagnostics bundle (trace id ranges, sample calls, and model/quantization flags).
- During the pilot, monthly financial remedy for any creditable availability/latency impact will be limited to a single flat credit equal to 10% of committed monthly spend.
- Post-pilot, we will run a joint excusal review. If FinPulse completes the agreed infra optimizations (list to be confirmed), we will revert to standard SLA bands without retroactive credits.

I attached an editable draft SLA (v3) with placeholders on telemetry and rollback. Laura — can you weigh in on whether the 10% cap is workable and how to surface carve-in language in the template? Connor, I opened an Ops ticket (OPS-1234) for the telemetry requirements.

1) Pilot period: 60 days beginning on the DocuSign execution date. During the pilot, p95 latency breaches defined in the agreed telemetry appendix between +20% and +40% will be treated as "operational degraded state" provided FinPulse supplies the diagnostics bundle for each incident.

5) Operational support: If FinPulse requests an expedited remediation, Redwood will offer a paid priority engineering path (terms to be reflected in Appendix B) — we will also include a route for non-financial remedies (engineering credits / priority tickets).
